newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Two charged with IRA murder of Irish policeman.
newsitem.headline: Two charged with IRA murder of Irish policeman.

text.p: Two men were charged on Wednesday with the IRA murder of an Irish policeman last year which shocked the nation and led to important clues on the guerrillas' arms dumps being given to security forces.

Jeremiah Sheehy of Rathkeale, 36, and Michael O' Neill, 46, were charged with the murder of policeman Gerry McCabe and the attempted murder of another police officer in a botched raid on a postal van in the southern town of Adare last June.
Police were escorting a post office van carrying cash when it was rammed by a four-wheel drive vehicle. McCabe was shot dead and the robbers fled empty-handed.
Sheehy and O'Neill had previously been charged with firearms possession with the intent to endanger life. Dublin's Special Criminal court remanded the pair in custody until October 7.

The murder of McCabe stunned Ireland. It was denounced by all political parties and security sources say they were given important information on IRA arms dumps by an outraged public which led to several important breakthroughs.
The Irish Republican Army, which is fighting to reunite British Northern Ireland with the Irish Republic, said its men had carried out the attack but it was not authorised.
IRA units regularly robbed Irish banks and shops in fund-raising raids in the 1970s and 1980s but had steered clear of the Republic in recent years.
